items.content_html:
Adds a programs.devenv NixOS module that installs devenv and sources its shell hook into bash/zsh/fish interactiveShellInit so trusted projects auto-activate on cd. It seems like NixOS does not have a programs.nushell like home-manager does, so I excluded it for now

This is the NixOS counterpart to the same module in home-manager (nix-community/home-manager#9379) and the pending one in nix-darwin (nix-darwin/nix-darwin/pull/1834), addressing cachix/devenv#3019

cachix/devenv#3019

Tested extensively by:

  2. Deploying to an aarch64-linux NixOS cloud VPS and configuring it as a Qdevice against a live Proxmox VE cluster.

Further care must be taken if DNS servers are received using DHCP and other dynamic host configuration tools.

items.content_html:
Another attempt at a module for https://github.com/vouch/vouch-proxy. Should address #299381 (comment).

The module is intended to run one instance of vouch-proxy per domain/app to be protected (that is, per entry in services.vouch-proxy.clients), as oauth2 clients should not be shared between applications. By default, it configures every nginx virtualHost matched by a services.vouch-proxy.clients.<name>.domain to use vouch-proxy.

Minimal working example below, where everything runs on the same host.
services.nginx.virtualHosts.myAppDomain1 and services.nginx.virtualHosts.myAppDomain2 are already defined as they would be without vouch-proxy, and with the clients myoauthclient1 and myoauthclient2 configured for vouch-proxy in the oauth2 provider.
This example uses kanidm, which the module takes care of (for every client) on vouch-proxy's side if kanidmUrl is set.
For other oauth2 providers, the correct auth_url, token_url and user_info_url need to be set either globally, under services.vouch-proxy.settings.oauth, or, if required (as is with kanidm for user_info_url), per client under services.vouch-proxy.clients.<name>.settings.oauth.

  services.vouch-proxy = {
    enable = true;
    kanidmUrl = config.services.kanidm.server.settings.domain;
  };

  services.vouch-proxy.clients = {
    myoauthclient1 = {
      port = 12345;
      domain = "myAppDomain1";
      environmentFile = "./myApp1.env"; # this file should contain `VOUCH_JWT_SECRET` and `OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`
    };
    myoauthclient2 = {
      port = 23456;
      domain = "myAppDomain2";
      environmentFile = "./myApp2.env";
    };
  };
